The foundational framework of multiagent systems integrates algorithmic methods, game theory, and logic into a coherent mathematical structure. Fictitious play provides a learning mechanism where agents iteratively refine their strategies assuming fixed opponent behavior, forming a basis for equilibrium analysis. Reinforcement learning extends this by allowing agents to learn optimal policies through interaction with uncertain environments. Distributed constraint satisfaction introduces coordination challenges among agents, modeled as shared variables and constraints. These primitives collectively enable GSI to perform Bayesian inference over agent beliefs and GSE to reason about evolving system states through structured interaction models.
